newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE "CLOSE TO FOREIGN TV DEAL".
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE "CLOSE TO FOREIGN TV DEAL".

text.p: England's top soccer league, the premier league, is close to signing a record-breaking deal for the television rights to foreign coverage of its matches, The Independent on Sunday newspaper said.

The paper said the premier league's chief executive, Rick Parry, "is understood to be in negotiations to quadruple football clubs' income from overseas TV rights to more than 20 million pounds ($32.8 million)".
It said Parry was keen to complete the deal before April when he moves to a new job as chief executive at Liverpool Football Club.

The paper said the league refused to confirm that talks were under way. It said the deal would be worth close to 25 million pounds, with around 20 million pounds going to the clubs after deductions -- giving qualifying clubs at least one million pounds a year for foreign rights to their games.
This compares with the 270,000 pounds a year each currently receives, the paper added.

The Independent on Sunday said that under the current contract, which is separate from a deal with British Sky Broadcasting to show live games in Britain, marketing rights to foreign TV companies are held by Rome-based marketing and sponsorship agency CSI.

A new contract is expected to be signed before the end of the current soccer season and would run until 2002. The new deal would not neccessarily be with CSI, with a number of other sports marketing agencies asked to tender for the rights, it said.
